doc.title: Barry Kernfeld interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 16, 2020

title: Introductions and a quip about the elusiveness of truth
summary: Rowe introduces Kernfeld as historian, author, piracy expert, saxophonist and archivist, and recalls an earlier Grove exchange.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe for the Fillius Jazz Archive at Hamilton College and I’m very happy to have Barry Kernfeld with me. And I’m going to introduce you, I’m not sure this would be the order of how you think of yourself, but a jazz historian, an author, an expert on song piracy, and a saxophonist. Does that work?
And an archivist these days. Yes.

Yes, an archivist. Okay. Well it’s a pleasure to talk to you and it’s curious, we had an exchange twenty plus years ago and I was able to write a few entries for your Grove at that time. And I’m wondering, we could talk about that for a minute. I found a quote from you from the edition twenty years ago, and it said, no actually it was the more recent, yeah, twenty years ago. You and your staff were reminded daily of the elusiveness of truth.
An appropriate comment in this current culture, eh?
Now that truth is lost altogether. But anyhow, sorry, I just went off on a tangent.
